What's the beta of Ethereum?¶

Sriram Susarla

2026-01-25

My research aim¶

The goal of this project is to manually calculate the beta of Ethereum. Beta is a metric of an assets volatility when compared to the 'market portfolio,' for which I use the SPY ETF. This project was inspired by section 12.11A of Melicher and Norton (2020)'s explanation of what beta is and how to estimate its value by doing a simple linear regression between market returns and asset returns. I additionally referred to Gundersen (2022) for the sake of learning about and using the idea of logarithmic returns in this project.

How do we interpret the beta?¶

The final calculated ETH beta (based on log returns) is 1.59. Interpreting this in the Capital Asset Pricing Model framework, this implies that ETH is highly linked with market movements and holding it amplifes the effect of market movements.

References¶

Gundersen, G. (2022, February 6). Returns and Log Returns. Gregorygundersen.com. https://gregorygundersen.com/blog/2022/02/06/log-returns/

Melicher, R. W., & Norton, E. A. (2020). Introduction to finance : markets, investments, and financial management. John Wiley & Sons.

In [4]:
#Get price data for each asset
ethdata <- tq_get("ETH-USD",
              from = "2020-01-01",
              to   = "2024-12-31"
                 )

spydata <- tq_get("SPY",
  from = "2020-01-01",
  to   = "2024-12-31"
)

#combine the datasets (based on SPY since it doesn't trade everyday)
combined <- inner_join(x=spydata, y=ethdata, by=join_by(`date`))
In [12]:
#calculate returns 
combined <- combined %>%
mutate( 
    `dailyReturnSPY` = (close.x - lag(close.x))/lag(close.x),
    `dailyReturnETH` = (close.y - lag(close.y))/lag(close.y)
    ) %>%
mutate(
    logreturnSPY = log(1 + `dailyReturnSPY`),
    logreturnETH = log(1 + `dailyReturnETH`)
)

#Basic Statistics 

#Preparing gt-table to work
gt_show <- function(gt_table){
   gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl(gt_table)
}
#Building a table of summary statistics 
tableBasicStats <- tibble(
    Statistics=c("Mean", "Median", "SD"), 
    `ETH Normal Returns` = 100*c(mean(combined$dailyReturnETH, na.rm = TRUE), median(combined$dailyReturnETH, na.rm = TRUE), sd(combined$dailyReturnETH, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `SPY Normal Returns` = 100*c(mean(combined$dailyReturnSPY, na.rm = TRUE), median(combined$dailyReturnSPY, na.rm = TRUE), sd(combined$dailyReturnSPY, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `ETH Log Returns` = 100*c(mean(combined$logreturnETH, na.rm = TRUE), median(combined$logreturnETH, na.rm = TRUE), sd(combined$logreturnETH, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `SPY Log Returns` = 100*c(mean(combined$logreturnSPY, na.rm = TRUE), median(combined$logreturnSPY, na.rm = TRUE), sd(combined$logreturnSPY, na.rm = TRUE)),
)

tableBasicStats %>%
  gt() %>% 
  fmt_number(
    decimals = 3
  ) %>% 
tab_source_note(
    source_note = "All values are percents."
  ) %>%
  gt_show()

The following visualization depicts the daily return of both ETH and SPY. We see that the daily change in price is on average much more intense than the market and appears to have somewhat of a correlation.

In [6]:
#compare returns 
returnscombined <- ggplot(
  data = combined |> 
    filter(between(date, as.Date("2021-06-01"), as.Date("2022-06-01"))),
  aes(x = date)
) +
  geom_line(aes(y = dailyReturnETH, color = "ETH")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = dailyReturnSPY, color = "SPY")) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Asset",
    values = c("ETH" = "red", "SPY" = "blue")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Return %",
    title = "Daily Return between June 2021 and June 2022"
  )

returnscombined

Following two visualizations depict the daily returns of ETH vs SPY, where each point depicts the return of a given day, with the y-coordinate being the ETH return and the x-coordinate being the SPY return.

The calculated beta, which is the slope of the line of best fit, is 1.50 for normal returns and 1.59 for log returns.

In [7]:
#Return ETH vs Return SPY 

returnsreturnsplot <- ggplot(data=combined, aes(x=`dailyReturnSPY`, y=`dailyReturnETH`)) + labs(x="SPY returns", y="ETH returns", title="ETH-SPY plot") + geom_point()
returnsreturnsplot <- returnsreturnsplot + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red")
returnsreturnsplot
model <- lm(`dailyReturnETH` ~ `dailyReturnSPY`, data=combined)
coef(model)
print("==================")
summary(model)

Following two visualizations depict a plot of Walmart vs SPY returns, as a comparison to the ETH one above.

We calculate a beta of 0.47 for normal returns and 0.46 for log returns.

In [9]:
#Load Walmart Data

wmtdata <-  tq_get("WMT",
              from = "2020-01-01",
              to   = "2024-12-31"
                 )
wmtspydata <- inner_join(spydata, wmtdata, by=join_by(`date`))
wmtspydata <- wmtspydata %>%
mutate( 
    `dailyReturnSPY` = (close.x - lag(close.x))/lag(close.x),
    `dailyReturnWMT` = (close.y - lag(close.y))/lag(close.y)
    ) %>% 
mutate(
    logreturnSPY = log(1 + `dailyReturnSPY`),
    logreturnWMT = log(1 + `dailyReturnWMT`)
)
